defect_observations.observation: The editorial warning def:p01-w02-p01-005-unbounded-warning speaks of 'The class {x:x notin x} of the warning in' sec:set-prerequisites-01, but the restored Warning 1.4 (handbook/restoration/inherited-00373-00405.tex lines 28-32 = frozen 400-404) names only the generic expression {x:P(x)}; the class {x:x notin x} does not occur anywhere in section 1.1. The cross-reference misdescribes the restored block. It should present {x:x notin x} as an instance of the warning's {x:P(x)}.

Section 1.1 prints no source or version attribution on its page. The part-level restoration layouts print 'Inherited source: Formal Logic, Version 1.0, source line N' (handbook/handbook.sty lines 1334-1335), but this ordinary scope prints nothing. In the reader, the only route to FLRV1 Version 1.0 is the citation of FrozenFormalLogicSetOperations in section 1.5 (sets-relations-functions-and-quotients-w02-p01-005.tex lines 15-17), whose bibliography note lists source lines 363-404 (handbook/bib/handbook.bib lines 13107-13121). This is not counted against the components. The bounded blocks carry no attribution of their own, and their definitional and cautionary standing is preserved exactly. It is recorded in case 'attributed standing' is meant to include on-page provenance.

Correctness, not coverage: the restored text is an unchanged transcription, and the provenance register records no layout changes, defect exclusions or variant links for units 9-13. So no authorized correction exists to identify. The equality clause of Definition 1.1 keeps definitional standing, although under the handbook's own convention it is extensionality plus substitutivity of identity. Definition 1.2 forms the power set by unbounded set-builder notation, which is what Warning 1.4 cautions against. The editorial section 1.5 states both points: the equality standing in def:p01-w02-p01-005-membership clause 3 (w02-p01-005 lines 52-57) and power-set existence by the power-set axiom (lines 184-187). The restored blocks themselves do not.
